## Read 3276 and 9ea3 properly instead of dispatching -- both far more advanced than 'in_progress' suggests

Applied the bff5 lesson (read COMMENTS, not the status field) before dispatching either. Both would
have been wasted dispatches:

 - 3276: 5 of 6 ACs done, 13 comments. AC6 landed as change 2549, AC5 as change 2586. The ONE
   remaining AC -- 'root usage has a bounded CEILING regardless of build burst rate' -- is epic 6202's
   deliverable, not this ticket's. It is blocked on S2-S5, three of whose siblings landed tonight. An
   agent sent at it would have found nothing to do, or worse, built a partial ceiling.
 - 9ea3: 3 of 5 done, 13 comments, the GATE_PEAK_RSS marker already landed in change 2589.

AND I ADVANCED 9ea3's AC5 MYSELF, because it is a [non-codebase] measurement AC satisfied by
recording figures in a comment -- tracker work, squarely mine. I had been collecting the data all
night incidentally from every gate run: ten GATE_PEAK_RSS samples.

The numbers are more useful than I expected:
 - plan_review peak ~714 MB (one sample). The epic sized on ~739 MB, so that estimate was sound and
   slightly conservative.
 - completion_verifier peak is remarkably TIGHT: nine samples, 418.2-440.4 MB, mean ~430 MB, spread
   under 6%.
 - The two gates differ by ~1.66x, so a single 'gate RSS' figure would overstate one and understate
   the other. Worth knowing before anyone sets a container mem_limit.
 - peak_delta_bytes was 0 on most closes and ~522 MB on the plan_review run, i.e. plan-review is where
   allocation actually happens; the close gate largely runs inside memory the process already holds.
 - Cross-check: S6's cap of 4 was derived as 4 x ~748 MB ~= 2.99 GB against ~3 GiB headroom. These
   samples support that for plan_review and show it is CONSERVATIVE for completion-verifier (~1.72 GB
   at four concurrent). So the cap is safe, and per-gate rather than global adjustment is what the
   data would support if it ever needs raising.

STATED WHAT IS STILL MISSING rather than ticking the AC: steady-state RSS per container is not
collected (needs the on-box container_memory_rss_bytes series), and how RSS scales with ticket size is
not collected -- every sample came from one store across ticket sizes I neither controlled nor
recorded, so I cannot honestly attribute the 418-440 MB spread to ticket size rather than noise.
Establishing that needs a deliberate campaign, not opportunistic collection. AC5 is PARTIALLY
satisfied and left unticked.
